links.label: USB-C: video + USB
links.evidence: The KVM's USB hub (with the Stream Deck Neo behind it) and the Odyssey both enumerate on the Mac mini, on a rear Thunderbolt port. Which rear port is not confirmed.

links.label: HDMI 4K60
links.evidence: Mac mini drives the Odyssey at 3840x2160 @ 60 Hz.
Stream Deck Neo enumerates behind the GenesysLogic hub. Which front port is not confirmed.
Enumerates on its own USB bus, one of the three rear Thunderbolt ports; the front ports sit behind Apple's built-in hubs and are empty. Which rear port is not confirmed.
Realtek 8156 enumerates at 5 Gb/s as en8 on a rear Thunderbolt port. Which rear port is not confirmed.
en8 negotiates 2500Base-T full duplex, and the router lists the adapter's MAC as a wired client of the office node. The switch port number is from the plan.

The NAS answers on SMB 445 and the router lists it as a wired client of the office node, the same side as the Mac mini. That it is plugged into the switch and not into the node, the port numbers and the 2.5G speed are from the plan.

links.label: 1G uplink
links.evidence: The router lists the Mac mini's adapter, the NAS and a TP-Link MAC as wired clients of the office node, so the office's wired gear hangs off that node. The port numbers are from the plan.

Not probed (the work MacBook is off limits). About an hour before the probe the router leased an address to a wired CE-Link Ethernet chip announcing the MacBook's name, which fits a dock in use then; at the probe it was gone.

links.risk: UGREEN says docks are unsupported on some of its other KVM models; not confirmed either way for this one.

links.evidence: Plan. A wired CE-Link Ethernet chip with the MacBook's name held a lease from 20:43 on 2026-11-20 but was not connected at the probe. That this chip is the ArcDock, and that it goes to the switch, is not confirmed.

links.label: Mesh backhaul, radio (5 GHz-2)
links.evidence: The node is a wireless client of the main router on 5 GHz-2 at -42 dBm (router client list). There is no cable between them.
The main router lists the bridge as a wired client. Which LAN port it uses is not confirmed.

links.label: Internet
links.evidence: The router's WAN port holds a public CableCo address by DHCP and the modem's page answers behind it, so this cable is in use and the modem is bridged. The modem's port name is from the plan.

openQuestions.text: A Mac at 10.20.0.98 is none of the three known ones. Is it Sam's? On that Mac: Apple menu, About This Mac, and System Settings, Wi-Fi, Details shows the address 10.20.0.98.
Is the iPhone named SamsPhone (iPhone 17 Pro Max) yours? Settings, General, About shows the name.
Which iPhone or iPad has the address 10.20.0.199? On Sam's iPhone: Settings, Wi-Fi, tap the (i) next to HomeNet, read IP Address.
One Tuya device is on the Wi-Fi near the office or bedroom. Open the Tuya or Smart Life app: which device is online? (Two MoesGo switch modules were bought in 2023.)
Do you own a reMarkable Paper Pro? A device calling itself imx8mm-example joins the Wi-Fi now and then. On the tablet: Settings, General, About.
Which MacBook Pro is the work laptop? Apple menu, About This Mac (size, chip, year).
What is the model number on the label under the UGREEN KVM?
What code is printed under the Spigen ArcDock (PD2302?), and is it the dock the work MacBook's network cable runs through?
What model is on the CableCo modem's label (for example Sagemcom F3896LG or Compal CH7465LG)?
Which Mediabox is it (Next, Next Mini, XL)? It is on the label underneath.
